---
title: Read predictions
description: "Run the saved model on request files, find each probability, and keep the identifiers you need to act on it."
---

A prediction request is a training record without its target. This page
scores the first model, whose output is small enough to read whole, then the
transaction model, whose output has one result per transaction.

## Score the first model

The [first model](your-first-model.qmd) reads `amount` and `merchant`. The
request file keeps those columns, omits `disputed`, and carries an identifier
to join the answer back:

```yaml
payment_id: payment-42
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
```

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.load("artifacts/payment.rf")
requests = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    predict="payments/requests.parquet",
    retain=("payment_id",),
)
result = model.predict(datamodule=requests, batch_size=256, devices=1)
```

`devices=1` collects one Arrow table on one device. `retain` copies the named
source columns into an `inputs` column; nothing else from the request is
echoed. One row of the result has this shape, with placeholders for the
numbers:

```yaml
inputs:
  payment_id: payment-42
predictions:
  disputed:
    state:
      valued: <probability>
      "null": <probability>
      padded: <probability>
      masked: <probability>
      other: <probability>
    content:
      probability: <probability of true>
    inferred: true
```

`content.probability` is the probability that this payment will be disputed.
`state` gives the probabilities of the five value states, and `inferred`
marks that this position was requested as a prediction; it is not a
confidence. To read the probabilities as Python values:

```python
rows = result.to_pylist()
probabilities = {
    row["inputs"]["payment_id"]: row["predictions"]["disputed"]["content"]["probability"]
    for row in rows
}
```

## Score the transaction model

The [transaction model](add-transaction-history.qmd) predicts every retained
transaction. The request keeps the `trxns` records, cut at the decision time
as in [Prepare observations](prepare-observations.qmd), and omits
`disputed` from each one:

```yaml
payment_id: payment-42
trxns:
  - booked_at: "2026-05-21T10:00:00"
    amount: 32.00
    merchant: Station Cafe
  - booked_at: "2026-05-27T18:15:00"
    amount: 56.20
    merchant: North Market
  - booked_at: "2026-05-28T14:30:00"
    amount: 84.50
    merchant: North Market
```

The same `predict` call returns `predictions.trxns`, a list with one result
per retained transaction in request order. Each item carries the same
`disputed` payload as above:

```python
observation = result.slice(0, 1).to_pylist()[0]
probabilities = [
    transaction["disputed"]["content"]["probability"]
    for transaction in observation["predictions"]["trxns"]
]
```

The list is as long as the retained history, not the branch cap: a request
with three transactions gets three results. With `overflow="tail"` and more
than 32 transactions, only the last 32 are retained and scored, so keep your
own transaction identifiers to match results to records.

## Read many rows at once

Converting to Python objects is fine for a few rows. For a whole request
file, keep the table columnar and let Polars flatten the nesting: each
`explode` turns a list into rows and each `unnest` turns a struct into
columns, following the record's shape from the outside in:

```python
import polars as pl

transactions = (
    pl.from_arrow(result)
    .select(
        pl.col("inputs").struct.field("payment_id"),
        pl.col("predictions").struct.field("trxns"),
    )
    .explode("trxns")
    .unnest("trxns")
    .unnest("disputed")
    .unnest("content")
)
```

`transactions` has one row per scored transaction with `payment_id`,
`state`, `probability`, and `inferred` columns, in request order. The same
expressions inside a [postprocessor](../guides/postprocessing.qmd) run on
every batch during batch inference and serving.

## Act on the result

Choosing a threshold is an application decision. A
[postprocessor](../guides/postprocessing.qmd) can turn the nested table into
flat decision columns, and the same processor serves batch files and the HTTP
deployment. For large request files, write results as they complete with
[batch inference](../guides/batch-inference.qmd); for online requests, see
[Serving](../guides/serving.qmd).

Two other columns can appear. `representations` holds exported embeddings
when a node has `embed=True`; see
[Reusable representations](reusable-representations.qmd). Nested targets,
structural nulls, and the full Arrow contract are described in
[Prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd).

Next, [evaluate](evaluation.qmd) the model against the review
process it is meant to support.
